name: Transition and Grid Resilience Strain
title: Global Power System · Transition and Grid Resilience Strain

definition.question: How strained is energy system resilience due to transition bottlenecks, grid constraints and climate stress on generation?
definition.low_end: Power system meets demand reliably with adequate firm capacity, grid, storage and interconnection to absorb weather and transition pressures.
definition.high_end: Systemic inability to meet demand due to combined grid bottlenecks, curtailment and climate-driven generation losses causing widespread outages and industrial shutdowns.

readings.rationale: Concurrent stress: Paks ~2000MW fell to 965MW then 240MW (~12%, one turbine) with Danube at record -106cm, Cernavoda one reactor offline with second scheduled, EDF shut 3 reactors (3.65GW) and reduced 7 others (~9% nuclear dip), EU hydro lowest in decade (-12% in 2025, -43TWh), wind -30-50% during heat dome, demand +20% on AC, evening peaks €285-326/MWh. No blackouts as of Aug 7 but voluntary…

Closest to 2026-10-01 at 68 (Paks 2000MW to 240MW at Danube -106cm, Cernavoda/EDF -9% nuclear, EU hydro -12%/-43TWh decade low, wind -30-50% lull, massive queues/curtailment, no blackouts). New UK wind/solar record 41% share (vs 25% gas), gas-fired -10% y/y, wind/solar +14%, avoiding £5.9bn gas (>100 LNG tankers, £1.3bn in Sep alone ~10TWh) partially offsets strain and explains electricity +4% vs…
